title: Radio sources near Gaia XP white-dwarf + M-dwarf candidates sit on faint neighbours 1-2 arcsec from the stars, and 39% of FaintQC candidates have a Gaia neighbour within 3 arcsec (matched stars: 13%)
abstract: Question: Do white-dwarf + M-dwarf (WD+MS) binaries, the hosts of known long-period radio transients and WD pulsars, emit at 144 MHz or 3 GHz more often than matched single stars, and can a catalogue cross-match find new such systems? Method: We matched 31,137 Gaia XP WD+MS candidates (Li et al. 2025; 1,649 CHI2 and 29,488 FaintQC) and 110,164 single Gaia DR3 stars matched in parallax, colour and absolute magnitude of the M-dwarf component to LoTSS-DR2, VLASS Epoch 1 and RACS-low. We also used 2,580 SDSS spectroscopic WD+MS binaries and 2,048 catalogued CVs and pre-CVs. Chance rates come from local source densities. We tested radio positions against Gaia DR3 and Pan-STARRS neighbours. Results: In LoTSS, 11 of 3,262 covered FaintQC candidates have a radio source within 2 arcsec against 2.5 by chance (p = 7e-5); controls give 8 against 7.5. The excess is only at 1-2 arcsec (10 against 1.9); within 1 arcsec, 1 is observed against 0.6 expected. Six of the 11 radio positions are 0.05-0.86 arcsec from faint Gaia sources (G = 20-22) and not on the stars, so they are background galaxies or AGN blended in BP/RP. In the full catalogue, 39.3 percent of FaintQC candidates have a Gaia neighbour within 3 arcsec against 13.1 percent of matched controls (12.8 percent after latitude re-weighting); half of the excess is resolved common-parallax main-sequence stars. Pan-STARRS gives 28 against 14 percent at 1-4 arcsec. CHI2 candidates also have an excess (32 against 15 percent). In VLASS, the only on-star CHI2 matches are the known AR Sco and WD J204259.71+152108.06. We find no new radio-emitting WD+MS binary. The 95 percent limit on steady on-star 144 MHz sources is 0.13 percent of FaintQC candidates (median 408 pc, L above about 9e16 erg/s/Hz). Limitations: Catalogue matching does not detect pulsed long-period transients (ILT J1101+5521 is not in the LoTSS-DR2 catalogue); neighbours fainter than G = 21 are not counted, so the blend fraction is a lower limit; the CfA VizieR mirror gave some empty responses, which we re-queried. Two nearby candidates (86 and 176 pc) remain open for polarisation follow-up.

display.caption: LoTSS-DR2 sources per ring around 3,262 Gaia XP FaintQC WD+MS candidates (blue) and 10,249 matched single stars (orange), observed divided by chance from the local density. The excess is only 1-2 arcsec from the stars. Error bars are Poisson.

Positions of LoTSS matches (< 2 arcsec) relative to the star (Gaia, moved to epoch 2017.5), with 1-sigma ellipses. Crosses are faint Gaia DR3 neighbours (G > 19.5); dotted lines join radio positions to them. The candidate radio sources sit on the neighbours.

Fraction of stars with a Gaia DR3 neighbour within a radius, for XP WD+MS candidates and matched controls. Left: common-parallax main-sequence neighbours. Right: neighbours without a matching parallax. Error bars are 2-sigma binomial.

citations.reason: Earlier campaign X-ray (eRASS1) test of Gaia WD-candidate binaries with matched controls; this work adds the radio band and a blend test for a different WD+MS selection.
Showed that offset background quasars produce false hot-companion signals in Gaia dwarfs; we find a similar blend effect in XP WD+MS selection.
